<explanation>
This project is reveal.js, an open source HTML presentation framework. It’s designed to let users create and deliver presentations on the web using plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Your system design diagram should capture the multiple layers and components that make up the framework, along with their interactions. Here’s how to approach drawing an accurate and detailed architectural diagram for reveal.js:

1. Identify the Main Components:
   • Core Engine: Represent the central JavaScript modules under the “js” directory (including controllers, components, and utilities). These modules manage slide presentation logic, navigation (e.g., keyboard, pointer, auto-animation), and layout.
   • Plugins: Show the “plugin” folder as a distinct component that extends functionality (e.g., Markdown support, syntax highlighting, math typesetting, speaker notes, search, zoom, etc.). Make sure to indicate that each plugin interacts with the core engine via a well-defined plugin API.
   • Theming and Styling: Include the “css” folder and its subdirectories (“theme”, “layout”, etc.), as these provide the presentation’s look and feel. Also, illustrate that the build process compiles these SCSS files into ready-to-use CSS files in the “dist” folder.
   • Build and Distribution: Highlight the “gulpfile.js”, “package.json”, and “dist” directory as representing the build system that transforms source files (SCSS, JS, assets) into a production-ready bundle.
   • Examples and Tests: Represent the “examples” and “test” directories as supporting components that illustrate usage scenarios and provide quality assurance through various demo presentations and tests.

2. Map Out the Relationships and Interactions:
   • Show directional relations from “Core Engine” (controllers and components) to “Plugins” to indicate that plugins both extend and hook into core functionalities.
   • Indicate interactions between the configuration files (like js/config.js) and the core modules, which manage presentation settings.
   • Represent data flow from the “css” theming layer to the Core Engine to illustrate that the presentation engine renders slides using the provided styles.
   • Highlight the build process flow: source code (JS, SCSS) → Gulp build (gulpfile.js) → output in the “dist” folder. This shows how the project is structured for deployment.
   • Include the direct integration or dependency of external libraries for features (for example, the math and markdown plugins, potentially using MathJax, KaTeX, or external syntax highlighters).

3. Note Key Architectural Patterns and Principles:
   • Modularity: Emphasize the decoupled design where plugins and core modules are kept modular and can be extended or replaced, reflecting a plug-and-play approach.
   • Separation of Concerns: Clarify that presentation logic, visual styling, and auxiliary features (like PDF export, notes, etc.) are separated into their own directories and modules.
   • Open Source Best Practices: Include elements for testing (see “test” directory) and example usage (see “examples” directory) which encourage quality and ease of contribution.

4. Tailor the Diagram to the Project’s Specific Structure:
   • For a presentation framework like reveal.js, your diagram should distinguish between the presentation “runtime” and the support layers (e.g., theming, plugins, build system).
   • Use different shapes or colors: You might choose one color or shape for JavaScript core modules, another for plugins, and yet another for static assets like CSS and HTML.
   • Add clear labels: For every component, provide names (for example “Core Controllers”, “Utility Modules”, “Markdown Plugin”, etc.) to ensure the diagram is self-explanatory.
   • Indicate directional arrows: Use arrows that clearly show data flow, such as:
       • “Configuration and Settings” => “Core Engine”
       • “Core Engine” ⇄ “Plugins”
       • “SCSS Source” => “Gulp Build Process” => “Compiled CSS”
       • “User Input (keyboard/touch)” => “Core Engine Controllers” => “Slide Transitions/Rendering”

5. Include Relevant Technologies and Frameworks:
   • JavaScript for core functionality and client-side interactions.
   • SCSS/CSS for styling and theming.
   • The build tool (Gulp) indicated by gulpfile.js.
   • External dependencies for features such as syntax highlighting and math rendering (highlight.js, MathJax/KaTeX) integrated via the plugins.

6. Final Guidelines for Crafting Your Diagram:
   • Break the diagram into clustered components that mirror the file structure (e.g., one cluster for “js” components, one for “css/theme”, one for “plugin” modules).
   • Use clear labels on each part; you might use rectangles for modules, circles for entry points (like “index.html” or “demo.html”), and arrows for dependencies and interactions.
   • Consider including a small legend or key for any colors or shapes used.
   • Ensure that you capture the modular interaction between the core presentation engine and its extension points (plugins, themes) along with the build and testing infrastructure.

By following these guidelines, you’ll create a detailed and accurate system design diagram that reflects the architecture of reveal.js and provides clear insights into how the presentation framework is structured, how its components interact, and how it is built for deployment. This level of detail will help stakeholders, developers, and contributors easily understand the system’s design and working principles.
</explanation>
